mindset: # Step 11 Gate 2 — EXECUTION INFRASTRUCTURE validation (NOT a scientific campaign)

This run validates ONE thing: that the real subprocess execution path — spawn, argv, sentinel/IPC, rlimits, cleanup — executes driven from the run's DECLARED COMPOSITION rather than from TIDMAD's import-time constants. The composed children must receive the transported physical data root and compose the run's declared metric, instead of silently falling back to defaults. Nothing about model quality is under test.
Propose ONE small, conservative, obviously-trainable model. Do not optimise for accuracy, novelty, or spectral coverage. Prefer the smallest architecture that honestly implements the task contract.

TWO outcomes waste this run, and both are avoidable. (1) A candidate that does not FIT: a pre-flight VRAM refusal burns an attempt without exercising any of the plumbing under test — this Gate runs under a HARD 4 GiB per-model VRAM allowance (operator decision, 2026-08-16). (2) An attempt refused before training by a runtime guardrail — a refused attempt trains nothing and produces no record, so keep the requested workload modest and accept the portions the launcher supplies rather than reaching for the full data scope.

Model QUALITY is explicitly NOT graded here, and neither are HealthGate verdicts, score magnitude, convergence or output diversity. A weak, collapsed or uninteresting candidate is ACCEPTABLE EVIDENCE for this Gate, because none of those things is what it is testing. Do not chase score improvements or loss-function tricks: propose the smallest honest model that trains, and report what it did.
This run is a SINGLE iteration with a SINGLE round. There is no cross-iteration state to carry and no follow-up experiment to set up. Report honestly on the one experiment that runs.
propose: HARD CONSTRAINT: the model must train and run inference within a 4 GiB GPU VRAM allowance. This is enforced by the production pre-flight — a candidate that exceeds it is refused and the Gate attempt is wasted.
Keep the model small: roughly 10k-500k parameters is appropriate for this validation. Do not exceed ~1M parameters.

Activation memory, not parameter count, is what refuses candidates: at a given segmentation_size, memory scales with depth x channel width. Prefer few layers and modest channel widths, and keep segmentation_size modest.

Concretely, prefer a shallow convolutional denoiser: on the order of 8-16 residual/dilated blocks with small channel counts. Do NOT propose 24+ block stacks, wide transformers, FNO/spectral pyramids, or multi-branch architectures.
Reuse a known-good compact baseline shape rather than inventing a new family. Novelty is explicitly not wanted in this run.
Batch size must be at least 4.

Avoid initialization or gating schemes that bias the output toward a constant: conservative near-zero residual scales and strongly negative gate biases have produced amplitude collapse on this budget. A plain residual convolutional stack is preferred over a gated/spectral one here.
implement: Implement exactly the proposed architecture, minimally and vectorised. No Python loops over the time dimension.
Honour the declared forward contract exactly.
tune: Use conservative, obviously-safe hyperparameters. This is a wiring validation, not a tuning study.

The 4 GiB VRAM allowance is hard. Do not increase segmentation_size, channel width, depth, or batch size beyond what was proposed. If an attempt is refused for memory, REDUCE capacity rather than retrying the same shape.

Accept the data portions the launcher supplies. Do not set trial, eval or train portions to 1.0 and do not request the full data scope: an attempt whose resolved optimizer-step count exceeds the runtime guardrail is refused before training and produces no record at all. The workload for this run is owned by the launcher, not by the plan.
